t: Amal Chandra Das v. State of West Bengal
m: Calcutta High Court · Decided · judgment stands
x: The 22 May 2024 judgment struck down the OBC classification of 77 classes made from 2010 and the OBC certificates issued on that basis, while protecting people already appointed. The State's appeals against it were withdrawn on 14 July 2026.

t: State of West Bengal v. Amal Chandra Das and connected appeals
m: Supreme Court of India · State and Commission petitions withdrawn 14 Jul 2026
x: The State and the West Bengal Commission for Backward Classes appealed the 2024 judgment. On 5 August 2024 the Court issued notice and asked the State to explain the survey and consultation behind the 77 designations. In March 2025 the State said the Commission was redoing the exercise, and on 6 November 2025 the Court told the High Court not to go ahead with the hearing until further orders. On 14 July 2026 the State and Commission petitions were withdrawn; other aggrieved parties may still pursue their own challenges.

t: NEET-UG and SLST candidates' category claims
m: Calcutta High Court · Petitions dismissed, Aug–Sep 2026

The Division Bench upheld the NEET-UG ruling on 18 August 2026, and the Supreme Court closed the challenge on 5 October 2026, saying the EWS benefit would be available next year.

t: Recruitment after the 2026 list: EWS moves, selected candidates and the new roster

t: 658-L / West Bengal Act VIII of 2026 (legislation)
x: The amendment revises the statutory definitions, reservation and sub-categorisation provisions, certificate requirements and schedules, and omits section 16. Percentage-setting and sub-categorisation require consultation with the Commission. Published on 15 July; brought into force on 27 July 2026 by BCW/15011/17/1579. The amendment does not itself publish a new class list or restore 17% reservation.

t: 659-L / West Bengal Act IX of 2026 (legislation)
x: The amendment revises member-secretary eligibility and tenure, and substitutes section 9 on inclusion requests, over-/under-inclusion complaints and ordinarily binding Commission advice. Published on 15 July; brought into force on 27 July 2026 by BCW/15011/18/1580. Read with the principal 1993 Act rather than treating the original text as the complete current statute.

t: BCW/15011/18/1580 (commencement notification)

t: 1060/Secy/BCW/7P-63/2024 (administrative)
x: BCW Department notification to all recruiting agencies on OBC reservation in recruitments already under way. Where appointment letters were already issued on a final merit list, the reservation policy in force at the time applies (10% OBC-A and 7% OBC-B, for processes begun before 22 May 2024 or between 10 June 2025 and 18 May 2026). All other cases follow Notifications 944 and 945 of 18 May 2026, read with the Labour Department roster notification Labr/85-Emp/EC/1M-01/2025 of 25 May 2026.

t: WBBPE Memo 3536/WBBPE/2026/59R-09/2024 (administrative)
x: West Bengal Board of Primary Education notice for the 2025 Assistant Teacher recruitment (Memo 2141 of 25 September 2025). A portal open from 14 to 31 October 2026 lets OBC-A and OBC-B applicants name their class if it is in the 66-class list of Notification 945, or move to Unreserved if it is not. Applicants who do nothing are treated as Unreserved, and an original OBC certificate is needed at verification.

t: WBBPE Memo 3747/WBBPE/2026/2024L-11/26 (administrative)

Because vacancies were revised after Notifications 944 and 945, a portal open from 5 to 9 November 2026 lets candidates with disabilities update their category, and also lets candidates who have not declared OBC status do so to claim OBC reservation. It comes after the High Court's 30 October 2026 order that the October window did not allow fresh applications.

t: Labr/85-Emp/EC/1M-01/2025 (administrative)
x: Labour Department Gazette notification (Kolkata Gazette Extraordinary, 25 May 2026) prescribing the revised Model 100-Point Roster of Vacancies after Notification 945-BCW. OBC now has 7 of the 100 points (points 9, 19, 29, 49, 59, 69 and 89; points 19 and 69 are for exempted-category OBC candidates and point 49 for an OBC ex-serviceman in Group-D posts), matching the 7% reservation. It also sets the EWS, SC, ST, disability, ex-serviceman and sportsperson points, and supersedes Labour Department Notification Labr/20-EMP/EC/1M-01/2025 of 27 January 2026.

t: 549-L (Bill No. 11 of 2026) (legislation)
x: Kolkata Gazette Extraordinary publishing the Bill to amend the West Bengal Backward Classes (Reservation of Vacancies in Services and Posts) Act, 2012. It renames the Act, defines OBCs by the 1993 Commission Act, lets the State fix the OBC percentage and any sub-categories only in consultation with the Commission (total SC, ST and OBC reservation not above 50%), and omits section 16 and Schedules I and III. These are the provisions the 2024 judgment struck down. The Bill became West Bengal Act VIII of 2026 (Notification 658-L of 15 July 2026), in force from 27 July 2026.

Iniquitous access to public and private banking institutions across Socio-Religious Communities (SRCs) can perpetuate disparities. This chapter analyses the extent to which the Muslim community has had access to the banking and credit facilities across various parts India during the recent five years. After a careful study of the Prime Minister’s 15-Point Programme in 44 minority concentration districts (59 bank branches) the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) found lack of thrust for increasing the credit flow to minority communities

It was stated at the outset that minorities have to grapple with issues relating to identity, security and equity. It was also recognized that these three sets of issues are inter-related. t: 2006 11 17 SACHAR Committee Report Muslim Social Economic Educational Status
